title: How to reduce interview no-shows
summary: Cut interview no-shows with timely confirmations, one-tap reschedule links, faster scheduling, and a respectful reminder cadence that keeps candidates engaged.

faq.a: Common causes are forgotten appointments, competing offers, unclear logistics, and a scheduling process that feels impersonal. Most are preventable with a confirmation step and a timely reminder.

faq.q: How far in advance should I send an interview reminder?
faq.a: A reminder roughly 24 hours before the interview, paired with a one-tap confirmation, gives candidates time to confirm or reschedule while keeping the interview top of mind.

faq.q: How do you calculate an interview no-show rate?
faq.a: Divide silent non-attendances by all completed bookings over the same period, and split it by interview stage and role family. High-volume roles typically run several times the rate of senior searches.

faq.q: Should a candidate get a second chance after a no-show?
faq.a: Yes, once. Offer a single easy rebook link with a warm note that assumes good faith. A second silent miss is the point to close the process respectfully.
